Intuitive Machines Inc (NASDAQ:LUNR) shares rose Wednesday, gaining about 5% as space stocks rallied on news of Space Exploration Technologies Corp.'s (NASDAQ:SPCX) planned financing for Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips.

The Financial Times reported that SpaceX is seeking about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt. The deal is led by Goldman Sachs, and Apollo Global Management is not involved.

Intuitive Machines is not connected to SpaceX through its lunar missions. The company launches on a rival provider's rockets, and investors have treated the two companies separately.

At publication, LUNR was up 5.2% at $14.85. SPCX was up approximately 3.5% on the day.
headline: Intuitive Machines Stock Jumps Wednesday as Space Stocks Rally
summary: Intuitive Machines rose about 5% to $14.85 as space stocks rallied, with SpaceX's financing led by Goldman Sachs and no Apollo role.
